Free values & meaning tools

20 short exercises on values & meaning, 2 to 10 minutes each, free and with no account needed. Open one and it runs right in the page.

The 20 tools

  • The values card sort

    Choose the five values that matter most to you from a long list, then rank them. A clear list makes daily decisions noticeably simpler.

    Card pick · 6 min

  • The life areas wheel

    Rate your satisfaction in eight areas of life. The shape that appears shows where things are full and where they have gone quiet.

    Dials · 4 min

  • Moments of meaning

    Write about times when life felt meaningful, then look for what they have in common. Meaning usually has a pattern, and the pattern is a map.

    Guided writing · 8 min

  • Where your time goes versus what matters

    Divide 100 points across how you actually spent your waking hours last week. Then hold it next to your values and see what the gap says.

    Budget · 4 min

  • A letter from five years on

    Write to yourself from five years in the future, from a version of you who came through what you are in now. It is a way of hearing what you already know.

    Guided writing · 10 min

  • Values you acted on this week

    Tick the things you actually did in the last seven days that expressed a value, even once and even small. Lived values are sometimes a different list from written ones.

    Noticing list · 3 min

  • What you want against what is expected

    Place the big shapes of your life on a grid of how much you actually want each one against how much it is expected of you. One corner is where quiet resentment grows.

    Grid · 6 min

  • Whose rule is it

    Sort the "shoulds" that follow you around by whether they match what you value or belong to someone else. A borrowed rule costs the same energy as one you chose.

    Sorter · 5 min

  • When the week feels like yours

    Mark the times across a typical week when what you are doing feels like it is genuinely yours. The slots are usually few, and they are worth protecting first.

    Week map · 3 min

  • What pride and regret point to

    Write about one thing you are quietly proud of and one you regret, then find the value underneath each. Both point at what matters, from opposite ends.

    Guided writing · 8 min

  • How far you have drifted from what matters

    Rate how often a set of signs of living off-course from your own values has been true lately. Drift is gradual, and nobody notices it from inside until it is pointed out.

    Reflection · 5 min

  • What "enough" looks like for you

    Set a dial for how close you feel to having enough in areas where "more" is the default. The dials sitting highest are where more will never quite land.

    Dials · 4 min

  • When nothing seems to matter

    Turn over cards that show a thought that flattens meaning, with a question and another angle on the back. Keep the ones that loosen something.

    Perspective cards · 5 min

  • The advice you keep giving

    The advice you repeat to friends is your values in their most honest form, because you give it without having to live it. Write it down, then turn it around.

    Guided writing · 6 min

  • Seven days of on purpose

    Each evening, rate how much of the day was chosen rather than drifted, how much of it mattered, and how much of it felt like you. Not how good it was; how much of it was yours.

    7-day log · 2 min

  • Put one value on the calendar

    Assemble a week with one small, real action for each of your values. A value with no slot in the calendar loses to whatever has one.

    Plan builder · 5 min

  • What you admire in the people you admire

    Think of a few people you admire and choose the qualities you admire most in them, then rank them. What you admire in others is what you value and may not yet give yourself permission to pursue.

    Card pick · 5 min

  • What you would give up last

    Rank a list of things by how hard you would fight to keep each one. What you would give up last is what you value most, whatever you would say if asked directly.

    Ranking · 4 min

  • A decision, held up to your values

    A short guided exercise for one live decision: walk each path six months forward, notice what your body does, and name what each path protects.

    Guided exercise · 7 min

  • Where meaning comes from

    Divide 100 points across the sources meaning actually came from in the last month, not where it is supposed to come from. One tall bar is a gift and a risk.

    Budget · 4 min

What these tools are, and are not

Every tool here is free and works without an account: choose cards, move dials, sort a list, follow a paced breath, or keep a seven-day log, and read back what you noticed at the end. They are built to make a vague feeling more specific, which is often the first useful step.

None of them diagnoses, screens for or treats anything, and nothing you see at the end is a score or a label. If something you notice worries you, a licensed therapist is the right next conversation, and the directory is free to browse.
